title: Four equivalent conditions for a morphism from the spectrum of a field to be of finite type

standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism from the spectrum of a field is quasi-compact because its source is a singleton, so finite type and locally finite type agree for it
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence of the first two conditions.

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebra lemma that a finite type domain extension inside a field has a localization that is a field with finite extension of the target field, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element whose localization turns the finite type injection into a finite field extension, giving the third condition.

standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter characterization of locally finite type morphisms on affine charts, and the algebra lemma that the image of a finite ring map into a field is a field over which the target is finite
standard_prerequisites.use: Give the implication from the third to the second condition, and the identification of the kernel of a finite ring map into a field as a maximal ideal.

core_obligations: Equivalence of (1) and (2): the source is a singleton, so any morphism from it is quasi-compact and finite type agrees with locally finite type (proof lines 3059-3061).

From (2) to (3): pick an affine open whose coordinate ring maps to the field by a finite type map, let p be the kernel so that the quotient embeds into the field as a finite type domain extension, apply the cited algebra lemma to find an element whose localization is a field with finite extension of the field, and lift that element to the coordinate ring so that the field becomes a finite module over that localization (proof lines 3063-3071).
From (3) to (2): a finite ring map on an affine chart is locally of finite type by the same-chapter characterization (proof lines 3073-3076).

From (3) to (4): for a finite ring map into a field the image is a field over which the field is finite, so the kernel is maximal, which says that the image point is closed with finite residue field extension (proof lines 3078-3082).
From (4) to (3): if the image is a closed point with finite residue field extension then the field is a finite module over the coordinate ring, which is the third condition (proof lines 3084-3086).
proof_roadmap: Dispose of the first equivalence by quasi-compactness of the singleton source (proof lines 3059-3061).

Reduce the locally finite type case to a finite ring map by localizing an affine chart along the kernel (proof lines 3063-3071), then identify the remaining conditions through the field-theoretic behaviour of a finite ring map into a field (proof lines 3073-3086).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent conditions on a morphism from the spectrum of a field to a scheme: being of finite type, being locally of finite type, being given by a finite ring map on some affine chart, and having closed image with finite residue field extension (statement lines 3043-3057). The counted proof is short but not a citation: it uses quasi-compactness of the singleton source for the first equivalence, the algebra lemma on finite type domain extensions inside a field to produce the localizing element that makes the field a finite module, and the field-theoretic behaviour of finite ring maps to close the remaining implications (proof lines 3059-3086). It is H2: each implication is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are elementary algebra.
